data.title: White House CEA to Launch Stablecoin Simulation Tool on Tuesday
data.description:
The White House Council of Economic Advisers will launch an interactive tool on Tuesday that lets users set parameters and run scenarios to support its conclusion that there is no material link between stablecoin growth and community bank deposit outflows. According to ChainCatcher, the move is aimed at helping Senate Republicans advance the CLARITY Act while addressing banking groups that said Monday the latest revisions still do not ease their concerns about stablecoin provisions.

Several Republican senators have signaled they may vote against the bill, while pro-crypto Democrats remain dissatisfied that the ethics provisions do not sufficiently constrain U.S. President Donald Trump. The bill needs at least 60 votes to advance.

data.title: Standard Chartered Sees Tokenized Stock Market Growing 250-Fold by 2028
data.description:
Standard Chartered said the tokenized stock market is expected to grow about 250-fold by 2028. According to Odaily, the bank said Arbitrum's business model could help traditional financial institutions move assets and operations onchain and benefit from the growth of tokenized stocks and other real-world assets.

As of early September, the tokenized stock market was worth about $2.9 billion and had become one of the faster-growing asset classes in the real-world assets sector.

data.title: Brightshore Capital Starts $250 Million Property Debt Platform
data.description:
Brightshore Capital, formerly GTIS Partners, has launched its first real estate debt investment platform with $250 million in initial capital, according to Bloomberg.

The global real estate firm said the platform comes as homebuilders’ financing needs are mounting.

data.title: Gold, Bitcoin Bets Diverge as Debasement Trade Splits
data.description: With Treasuries sinking and the dollar falling this year, Bitcoin and gold are again being touted as hedges against currency debasement, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Radiant World, Sapphire Minmetals Trim Staff as Fraud Allegations Grow
data.description:
Radiant World and Sapphire Minmetals have made further job cuts across their offices in Asia and Europe as allegations of fraud mount, according to people familiar with the matter.

Bloomberg reported the two iron ore traders are under pressure amid the legal challenges.

data.title: Seres and Huawei to Shift Aito Cooperation Toward Seres-Led Operations
data.description:
Seres and Huawei will adjust their Aito smart-car partnership this week, with product, marketing, sales and service shifting from Huawei-led to Seres-led operations while Huawei provides support, according to Jiemian News. The report said Harmony Intelligent Mobility Alliance will direct more resources to Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie.

The change would give Seres more control over Aito pricing, technology procurement and service spending. Jiemian News said Seres has already been preparing for a more flexible, asset-light model through new projects such as AIVA, where Seres subsidiary Saidu Technology has worked with Volcano Engine on large-model and smart-cockpit technology.

Seres reported revenue of 57.493 billion yuan in the first half of 2026, with a net loss attributable to shareholders of 1.717 billion yuan. Sales expenses were 8.471 billion yuan and R&D spending was 3.734 billion yuan. The company said impairment charges reduced net profit attributable to shareholders by about 1.751 billion yuan, as revenue from existing models fell short of expectations amid technology upgrades.

Jiemian News said Seres has been paying both for Huawei's technology and services and for its own R&D and distribution network. Under the new arrangement, Seres may buy more functions on demand, including intelligent driving, smart-cockpit systems and sales services, while keeping more of the related decision-making in-house.

data.title: PREMARKET MOVES | Dave & Buster's Falls 17% on Q2 Miss; Enova Drops 15% After Withdrawing Grasshopper Bancorp Applications
data.description: According to CNBC, Dave & Buster's Entertainment shares plunged 17% in premarket trading after the arcade and restaurant company's second-quarter results disappointed investors. Reported revenue of $544.1 million missed the $556.8 million FactSet consensus estimate, and adjusted EBITDA of $98.9 million missed the expected $120.4 million. The company posted an unexpected adjusted loss of 27 cents per share, missing the 18 cents profit per share expected by analysts polled by FactSet. Enova International tumbled more than 15% after the online provider of loans and credit services said it is withdrawing its regulatory applications for the proposed acquisition of Grasshopper Bancorp; it reaffirmed third-quarter and full-year guidance and announced an intention to accelerate share repurchases. Sysco slid nearly 2% after the wholesale distributor to restaurants, hospitals and schools announced a common stock offering of 12.3 million shares priced at $81 per share. Etsy rose 3% after Oppenheimer upgraded the online marketplace to outperform from perform, saying it will likely get a boost from artificial intelligence for virtual shopping, and set a $90 price target suggesting 21% upside from Monday's close.

data.title: Brazil’s Low Valuations Spur More Stock Delistings
data.description:
Depressed valuations and stagnant trading volumes are pushing more companies to go private in Brazil, according to Bloomberg.

The trend is further reducing Brazil’s share in global equity portfolios.

data.title: Dave & Buster's, Enova, Sysco And Etsy Move Before The Bell
data.description: According to CNBC, Dave & Buster's Entertainment shares fell 17% after the arcade and restaurant company reported second-quarter results that missed Wall Street estimates, including revenue of $544.1 million versus the $556.8 million FactSet consensus, adjusted EBITDA of $98.9 million versus $120.4 million expected, and an adjusted loss of 27 cents per share versus expectations for a profit of 18 cents per share. Enova International dropped more than 15% after the online lender said it is withdrawing its regulatory applications for the proposed acquisition of Grasshopper Bancorp, while reaffirming third-quarter and full-year guidance and saying it intends to accelerate share repurchases. Sysco slipped nearly 2% after the wholesale distributor announced a common stock offering of 12.3 million shares priced at $81 per share. Etsy rose 3% after Oppenheimer upgraded the online marketplace to outperform from perform and set a $90 price target, saying it is likely to benefit from artificial intelligence for virtual shopping.

data.title: AI | TSMC Co-COO Says AI Is Like a ‘Three-Year-Old Superman’
data.description:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. co-COO said the company is cautious about using AI, likening the technology to a toddler with extraordinary powers that does not know right from wrong, according to Bloomberg.

The executive used the comparison to explain TSMC’s approach to AI.

data.title: STOCKS | John Murphy Sees Hybrid Vehicles Reaching 34% of U.S. Market by 2030
data.description:
Automotive analyst John Murphy released his latest outlook on the U.S. auto market on Tuesday. According to Sina Finance, he said the chances of Chinese automakers entering the U.S. market are low in the short term, and he expects hybrid vehicle demand to surge over the next four years, with hybrids reaching 34% of the market by 2030.

Murphy also said U.S. lawmakers have little willingness to approve such a move, citing concerns about pressure on U.S. automakers and the domestic auto industry. He added that even if Chinese automakers were to build factories in the United States, allowing them to enter the market without restrictions would still have a major impact on the industry.

According to the report, the U.S. Commerce Department said that starting next year, automakers will be barred from importing or selling vehicles in the United States that use technology developed or produced by Chinese companies. Murphy also said that, over the next decade, 5 to 10 of the brands currently sold in the U.S. market could exit, and he identified Polestar, Maserati, Alfa Romeo, Jaguar, and Fiat as the five brands most likely to leave U.S. sales.

Murphy said demand for conventional hybrids that do not need external charging and offer strong fuel economy is popular with mainstream consumers. J.D. Power data showed that hybrids accounted for more than 18% of vehicles sold in the U.S. market in January-July. He also said U.S. battery-electric vehicles are likely to see only modest growth before 2030, and that the industry is facing a sharp slowdown in new-model launches in 2026-2028.

data.title: Ondo Finance Plans Private Forums in Singapore and Seoul During TOKEN2049 and Korea Blockchain Week
data.description:
Ondo Finance said it will accelerate its expansion in the Asia-Pacific market by hosting private forums during Korea Blockchain Week in Seoul and TOKEN2049 in Singapore. The company said the events are intended to bring together influential regional institutions and industry voices as it seeks to strengthen its position in the Asia-Pacific institutional market.

According to Foresight News, Ondo will hold a private forum called "Open Interest" in Singapore on October 6 during TOKEN2049. Ondo Perps CEO and its strategy team will present product direction and views on industry trends, followed by a panel discussion with institutional experts. Confirmed attendees include Franklin Templeton, SGX Group, Siam Commercial Bank, and Ericsenz Capital, while existing partner SBI Holdings will also attend.

Ondo will also host a private forum during Korea Blockchain Week. Existing partner Mirae Asset Global Investments has confirmed attendance, and the company has invited institutional guests including Hanwha Asset Management and Meritz Securities, along with crypto industry voices Fireant and WeCryptoTogether.

data.title: Eclat Health Weighs India IPO to Raise Up to $300 Million
data.description: Eclat Health Solutions is considering an initial public offering in India that could raise as much as $300 million, people familiar with the matter said, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Schroders Cuts WuXi XDC Stake Below 5%
data.description:
Schroders reduced its holding in WuXi XDC Cayman (02268) by 680,000 shares on Friday (the 11th), at an average price of HK$71.3591 per share, for proceeds of HK$48.5242 million, according to ETNet.

Its stake fell to 4.98% after the sale.

data.title: S&P Global Ratings Sees Broader Auto Industry Restructuring Ahead
data.description:
S&P Global Ratings said GAC Group (2238) and FAW Group have reached a deal at a critical time, as weak domestic demand, excess capacity and the rapid shift to electric vehicles continue to pressure state-owned automakers and their joint ventures with foreign carmakers, according to Ming Pao.

The agency expects the industry to see a broader wave of restructuring over the next two to three years.

data.title: CNBC Fed Survey: Majority Now Forecast At Least Two Rate Hikes Over Next Year
data.description:
According to CNBC, a majority of respondents to the CNBC Fed Survey now expect at least two Federal Reserve rate hikes over the next year, while 55% forecast more than one increase. That marks a sharp shift from last month, when 46% expected a hike ahead, and the share has risen to 86%.

The survey found that respondents now see inflation as broader than energy prices after Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish Jackson Hole speech, oil prices surged and inflation failed to cool. Most of the 29 respondents, including economists, fund managers and strategists, said the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed at least a month longer and that oil prices will stay elevated for more than six months. CPI forecasts rose for both 2026 and 2027, with the average forecast near 3.5% for this year and 2.85% in 2027.

The Fed is set to decide on rates Wednesday at the end of its two-day meeting. Despite the shift toward multiple hikes, respondents left the growth outlook little changed, with recession odds at an average 29% over the next 12 months, GDP seen around 2.25% this year and next, and unemployment expected near 4.25%. The S&P 500 is forecast to hold its current level through year-end and rise 8% to 8,274 next year.

data.title: DBS, OCBC and UOB Complete First Singapore Dollar Tokenized Deposit Payment on Swift Ledger
data.description: DBS, OCBC and UOB have completed a local Singapore dollar tokenized deposit payment on the Swift blockchain ledger, marking the first interbank tokenized deposit transaction among the three institutions. According to Odaily, the banks had previously completed cross-border transactions on Swift Ledger. After local interoperability was established, corporate clients can complete tokenized payments across institutions.

data.title: KRX After-Hours Trading Sees Heavy Volume, Volatility on First Day
data.description: According to The Korea Herald, volatility rose and price control mechanisms were triggered at a much higher level on the first day of after-hours trading on the Korea Exchange (KRX), the bourse operator said Tuesday. The KRX launched the session from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. Monday to boost global competitiveness and widen trading opportunities for investors. A total of 72.24 million shares worth 1.8 trillion won (US$1.3 billion) changed hands during the four-hour session, compared with some 905 million won in the previous benchmark period.

data.title: Bitcoin Needs $82,877 to Offset Expected Mining Difficulty Increase
data.description:
Bitcoin would need to rise to approximately $82,877 to offset a projected 4.6976% increase in mining difficulty. According to NS3.AI, the estimate is based on a BTC price of $79,158.

The next mining difficulty retarget is expected around 05:42 UTC on Sept. 19. A separate estimate projected a 5.26% increase.

data.title: Balancer Considers Phased Shutdown After v3 Exploit and $130 Million Losses
data.description:
Balancer is considering a phased shutdown after an exploit hit its v3 protocol and caused almost $130 million in losses. According to NS3.AI, Balancer Labs CEO Marcus Hardt proposed distributing the project's $9 million treasury to BAL holders.

The proposal would move all pools to withdrawal-only mode on October 30.
